Rarity.rationale: ThrowingAxe.cs:12. Granted by the ported Tanx shrine (events/tanx.py:13). Executed: `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b16.py pool` -- Ancient rarity is not in the grab bag, the shrine is the only path.

AfterRoomEntered.rationale: See guard N3. C# clears UsedThisCombat at AfterRoomEntered for a CombatRoom (ThrowingAxe.cs:27-36); the sim clears it at on_combat_start, which is the very next combat-entry step (CombatRoom.cs:225-231 runs SetUpCombat -> Hook.AfterRoomEntered -> AfterCombatRoomLoaded, and BeforeCombatStart sits inside the last of those). Nothing can read the flag in between, because the only reader is ModifyCardPlayCount and no card can be played before the first turn opens. Recorded as a divergence rather than faithful because the slot genuinely differs -- this is the reset site `sweep-reset`'s C# census was extended to cover after batch 12 found `permafrost` there.

ModifyCardPlayCount.maps_to: modify_card_play_count (throwing_axe.py:30-36), dispatched by HookSystem.modify_card_play_count (hooks.py:224-234) from CombatState._resolve_card_play (combat.py:469-471)
ModifyCardPlayCount.rationale: ThrowingAxe.cs:38-49: bail if UsedThisCombat, bail if the card is not the owner's, else `playCount + 1`. throwing_axe.py:33-36 mirrors the used-this-combat bail and the +1; the owner clause is guard N1 (multiplayer). The +1 is a literal on both sides with no DynamicVar and no ascension branch. Executed slot check: hooks.modify_card_play_count is consulted once per play at combat.py:469, on the value `1 + card.base_replay_count`, which is C#'s `GetEnchantedReplayCount() + 1` (CardModel.cs:2017).

AfterModifyingCardPlayCount.maps_to: collapsed into modify_card_play_count -- `self.used_this_combat = True` is set at throwing_axe.py:35, inside the modifier, before the +1 is returned
AfterModifyingCardPlayCount.rationale: See guard N2, which settles the collapse by execution: C# only calls AfterModifyingCardPlayCount on the models whose return actually CHANGED the count (Hook.cs:1372-1385 builds `modifyingModels` from `num != num2`), and Throwing Axe always changes it, so 'set the flag inside the modifier' and 'set it in the follow-up hook' are the same thing for this relic. The sim's own docstring says as much (throwing_axe.py:15-17) and it is right -- checked against PROMPT.md bug class 24.

AfterCombatEnd.maps_to: no counterpart; on_combat_start (throwing_axe.py:27-28) is the only reset
AfterCombatEnd.rationale: ThrowingAxe.cs:59-64 clears UsedThisCombat a second time at combat end, which is redundant with the AfterRoomEntered clear by construction -- the relic's only other hook is a combat hook, so nothing reads the flag between the two points. The sim keeps one reset at combat start and reaches the same observable state everywhere either codebase can be observed. Same shape and same verdict as relic/unsettling_lamp's AfterCombatEnd (binding rule 3), and the contrast with relic/belt_buckle -- which dropped BOTH resets and is live -- is why this one is a divergence.

guards.what: N1: `card.Owner != base.Owner` (ThrowingAxe.cs:44-47) has no sim counterpart, and the sim sets its used-flag BEFORE the point where that check would have bailed
guards.rationale: Multiplayer-only owner disambiguation. The shared contract lists multiplayer-only params as out of scope; the sim's single Player makes the check structurally true. The ordering detail matters only in multiplayer: throwing_axe.py:35 latches used_this_combat and then returns count + 1, so if a second player's card ever reached the hook the sim would spend the charge on it. Single-player, every card in CombatState belongs to the one player. Waived with the reason named.

guards.what: N2 (EXECUTED): the collapse of ModifyCardPlayCount + AfterModifyingCardPlayCount into one sim method could burn the charge on a non-play query -- it does not
guards.rationale: CardModel.cs:2010-2013 warns in so many words that GeneratePlayCount runs a state-modifying hook and so 'you can only run this method in situations where it's okay to modify combat state (i.e. not as part of previews)'. That is the risk the sim's collapse creates: any read-only caller of hooks.modify_card_play_count would silently spend Throwing Axe. `grep -rn 'modify_card_play_count' sts2_rl/` finds exactly two callers -- combat.py:469 (a real play) and cards/drum_of_battle.py:48 -- and the second is faithful too: DrumOfBattle.cs:31-41 calls `GeneratePlayCount(base.CombatState, null)` from its own AfterCardExhausted, which fires Hook.AfterModifyingCardPlayCount and so spends Throwing Axe in the game as well. The sim's previews.py does NOT consult this hook (its damage preview calls modify_hp_lost with no modifiers list, previews.py:82). So there is no preview path and the collapse is safe. Rule 7: combat.py, cards/drum_of_battle.py, previews.py and CardModel.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: the reset trace required by PROMPT.md bug class 13 -- C# resets at AfterRoomEntered AND AfterCombatEnd, the sim only at on_combat_start
guards.rationale: TRACE: the only reader of used_this_combat is modify_card_play_count, which is reached only from a card play (N2). on_combat_start runs at combat.py:208, the last statement of CombatState.__init__, i.e. before the first player turn and therefore before any card can be played -- executed reference `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order` prints on_combat_start ahead of on_block_cleared(turn=1). So the flag is False at every moment a reader can see it, and this relic is the `art_of_war` shape rather than the `belt_buckle` shape. `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` does not list throwing_axe at all, which agrees. Recorded because sweep A defect 6 (AfterRoomEntered omitted from the C#-side census) means an earlier sweep would have printed 'C# resets: NONE' for exactly this relic; the reset is real and the port does honour it.
